testCases.title: Guest Checkout - Validate Email Format in Address Form
testCases.failedAssertion: [DOM] Email format error rendered for each invalid pattern — 'user@domain' (no TLD) did not trigger validation error
testCases.notes: Patterns 1 ('notanemail') and 2 ('user@') correctly show error 'Enter a valid email address'. Pattern 3 ('user@domain' — no TLD) shows NO validation error; the form field accepts it as valid. HTML5 email validator in Edge/Chromium accepts 'user@domain' without TLD, so client-side validation does not fire for this pattern. The assertion requires an error for all three invalid patterns.

bugs.title: No 'Create Account' prompt shown on guest checkout confirmation page
bugs.failedAssertion: [DOM] Create Account prompt visible on confirmation page
bugs.stepsToReproduce: 1. Navigate to storefront as guest (not logged in). 2. Add a product to cart. 3. Fill shipping address, select delivery method and payment method. 4. Place order. 5. Observe /checkout/completed page.
bugs.expected: A 'Create Account' prompt or banner is displayed on the confirmation page, offering the guest the option to register and link the order to a new account.
bugs.actual: Confirmation page shows only 'SHOW ORDER' and 'HOME PAGE' buttons. No 'Create Account' or registration prompt is present for guest users after order placement.

bugs.title: Guest address email field accepts 'user@domain' (no TLD) as valid — no validation error shown
bugs.failedAssertion: [DOM] Email format error rendered for 'user@domain' (no TLD) pattern
bugs.stepsToReproduce: 1. Navigate to /cart as guest. 2. Click 'select a shipping address'. 3. In the 'New address' dialog, enter 'user@domain' in the Email field. 4. Tab out of the field. 5. Observe whether a validation error appears.
bugs.expected: An error message such as 'Enter a valid email address' is shown for 'user@domain' (no top-level domain).
bugs.actual: No validation error is rendered. The form accepts 'user@domain' as a valid email format. The HTML5 browser validator in Edge/Chromium does not reject addresses without a TLD.
